content: Lindane is a medication used to treat lice and scabies, but it carries significant risks of severe side effects, including seizures and death. Safer alternatives are available, and lindane should only be used if other treatments are ineffective or cannot be used. Individuals at higher risk for serious side effects include infants, children, older adults, people weighing less than 110 pounds, and those with skin conditions such as psoriasis, rashes, or broken skin. Lindane must not be used in premature infants or individuals with a history of seizures, particularly if the seizures are difficult to control. Lindane is toxic if overused or applied for too long. It is crucial to follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Do not use more than the prescribed amount, do not leave it on longer than directed, and do not repeat the treatment even if symptoms persist. Itching may continue for weeks after the lice or scabies are eradicated. Lindane is available as a lotion for scabies and a shampoo for lice. It is a scabicide and pediculicide that kills lice, scabies, and their eggs. When using lindane lotion for scabies: If you bathe or shower, wait one hour before applying the lotion to allow your skin to cool. Shake the lotion well before use. Use a toothbrush to apply the lotion under your fingernails, then discard the toothbrush. Do not use it for brushing your teeth. Apply a thin layer of lotion from your neck down to your toes, including the soles of your feet. Do not use more than necessary. Dispose of the bottle and any leftover lotion safely, keeping it out of reach of children. Wear loose-fitting clothing and avoid tight or plastic clothing. Do not use plastic-lined diapers on treated infants. Avoid skin contact with others during this time to prevent harm to them. After 8–12 hours, wash off the lotion with warm water (not hot water). When using lindane shampoo for lice: Wash your hair with regular shampoo at least one hour before applying lindane and dry it thoroughly. Do not use conditioners or oils. Shake the shampoo well and apply just enough to wet your hair, scalp, and the small hairs on the back of your neck. For pubic lice, apply to the pubic area and underlying skin. Dispose of the bottle and any leftover shampoo safely. Leave the shampoo on for exactly 4 minutes, keeping your hair uncovered. Do not exceed this time, as it increases the risk of seizures and other severe side effects. After 4 minutes, lather the shampoo with a small amount of warm water and rinse thoroughly with warm water. Dry your hair with a clean towel and use a fine-tooth comb or tweezers to remove lice eggs (nits). Assistance may be needed for head lice. Lindane should not be used for any other purposes. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before using lindane, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, as some may interact with lindane. Notify your doctor if you have a history of seizures, brain or spinal tumors, head injuries, liver disease, HIV/AIDS, or if you consume large amounts of alcohol or have recently stopped drinking or using sedatives. Breastfeeding mothers should pump and discard their milk for 24 hours after using lindane and feed their baby with stored milk or formula during this time. If you have scabies or pubic lice, inform your doctor about your sexual partner, as they may also need treatment to prevent reinfection. For head lice, all household members or close contacts may require treatment. Do not share your medication with others, as it may harm them. Continue your normal diet unless otherwise instructed by your doctor. Minor side effects of lindane may include skin rash, itching, burning, dryness, numbness, tingling, or hair loss. Severe side effects, such as headache, dizziness, drowsiness, uncontrollable shaking, or seizures, require immediate medical attention. Report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch program. Store lindane in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, consulting your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the individual has collapsed or is not breathing. If lindane is accidentally ingested, seek emergency assistance immediately. If it gets into the eyes, rinse with water and seek medical help if irritation persists. Keep all medical appointments and do not allow others to use your medication. Lindane prescriptions are not refillable. If additional treatment is needed, consult your doctor. Lindane is also known as benzene hexachloride or gamma hexachlorocyclohexane.
